things.note: Side view of a small pink hull with a pale blue cabin, floating on the water surface.
Cross-section with the upper canal stepped well above the lower canal; an 'UPHILL' arrow arcs from boat to upper level.
Cross-section of a walled chamber between lower and upper canals, with gate posts; small 'CHAMBER' label but the structure reads on its own once gates are in.
Flat tan/khaki rectangles stand for the water, while the ground beneath is pale blue; the colours read backwards (water looks like earth), so it is known only from the boat floating on it.
A thin dark vertical bar with a 'GATES' label; no gate leaves or hinges.
A thin dark vertical bar between chamber and upper canal.
A tiny pale notch in the upper gate bar with a dashed line and 'SLUICE' label; would not be known without the label.
Chamber water top and upper canal water top sit level, with a dashed guide line.

changes.change: the lock lifts the boat using water
changes.note: Narrated in sheets 2 and 3 while the picture is static; the lift itself is shown later when the chamber fills.
Boat slides right from the lower canal into the chamber (7.2 to 8.0 s).
A dark bar rises/fades in between lower canal and chamber (9.2 to 9.7 s); appears rather than swings shut.

changes.change: sluice in the upper gate opens
changes.note: A small pale gap appears in the upper gate bar at about 12.7 s; very small, mostly carried by the label.
A curved stream arcs from the sluice into the chamber and the chamber fill rises.
Chamber water level rises from lower-canal height to upper-canal height (14.5 to 20 s) and the boat rides up on it.
Chamber surface reaches the upper canal surface and the pouring stream stops (about 20.7 s).
The upper gate bar disappears at about 25 s, a sheet after it is narrated (sheet 12, where the bar is still in place).
Boat slides right from the chamber into the upper canal (25 to 26 s).
